subject: SLA redlines: staggered maintenance window & credit-scaling proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: SLA: uptime & maintenance windows — initial redlines

Marcus,

Thanks for the draft Order Form and SLA. Procurement and Engineering at Acme reviewed and pushed a few redlines we need to get in place before we can sign. High level asks: 99.99% uptime for production endpoints, a credit scale that escalates beyond the typical quarterly cap if cumulative downtime exceeds 72 hours, and maintenance limited to weekends with at most 8 hours per quarter for disruptive upgrades. We also want guaranteed P1 response within 30 minutes and a defined emergency maintenance playbook.

I attached our redline (Acme_SLA_redlines_20261110.pdf) with inline comments. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a staggered maintenance window model (regional maintenance windows that do not overlap across Acme production regions)? That would help us with our multi-region failover.

If needed, we can schedule a 30m call this week — our lead SREs are available Wed/Thu afternoons EST.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jensen
Head of Procurement
Acme Corporation

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime & maintenance windows — initial redlines

Sarah — thanks for the detailed redline. Appreciate the clarity. Quick summary of what we can do vs what we need to clarify: 

- Uptime: We usually offer 99.95% for hosted endpoints and 99.99% when customers take dedicated capacity with a commitment level. For the Order Form I can propose a two-tier SLO: 99.99% for dedicated (Committed Capacity) and 99.95% for multi-tenant hosted API. If Acme will commit to a Dedicated pool (we can model quantity and sizing), we can mirror the 99.99% target.

- Credit escalation: We are open to a credit-scaling model tied to cumulative downtime in a rolling 90-day window rather than a hard quarterly cap. Legal will need to cap total credits as a percentage of spend; lauren, can you weigh in on a reasonable cap while allowing an "exception" clause if outages exceed 72 hours cumulative and are not covered by exclusions?

- Maintenance windows: Staggered regional maintenance is feasible operationally. We can commit to providing 48–72 hours advanced notice for standard maintenance and to limit disruptive maintenance to a combined 8 hours per calendar quarter per region. For emergency maintenance (security incidents), we propose a separate, faster notification path and short windows with failover guidance.

- Response SLAs: For P1s we typically guarantee an initial response (acknowledge + mitigation plan) within 60 minutes; 30 minutes is aggressive for our hosted tier but we can aim for 30 minutes for Dedicated with a stronger SOC and an on-call rotation guarantee.

Next steps I propose: 1) lauren and kim to provide redline language for the credit cap + exception path, 2) I’ll draft an Order Form snippet showing dedicated vs hosted SLOs and a maintenance matrix, 3) schedule a 30m review with Acme SREs — Wed 14:00–15:00 EST or Thu 15:00–16:00 EST work for me.

I attached RW_SLA_proposal_v3_redline.docx with the suggested text for the Order Form.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime & maintenance windows — initial redlines (legal notes)

Thanks for the summary, Marcus. Sarah — appreciated the redline. A few legal notes / proposals below (high-level):

1) Credit cap and exception clause: We can set a default cap at 100% of the monthly invoice for the affected service in the 12-month period, with an explicit exception that allows additional credits beyond the cap if cumulative unplanned outage exceeds 72 hours in any rolling 90-day window and Redwood confirms the outage was not caused by Customer misconfiguration or third-party upstream providers. We will require post-incident root cause analysis before any exception credits are issued.

2) Definitions and carveouts: Tighten definitions for "maintenance", "emergency maintenance", "downtime", and "service affecting". Propose to include an explicit list of customer-configured features that are excluded (e.g., customer-managed plugins, third-party connectors).

3) Notice windows: We can accept 48 hours for standard maintenance notice; for larger disruptive changes (schema-affecting, data migrations) we prefer 72 hours. Emergency maintenance (security/critical fixes) will be described in the Order Form with an expedited notice and documented justification.

4) Response time commitments: I recommend keeping acknowledge time at 60 minutes for hosted and 30 minutes for Dedicated. If Acme requires 30 minutes across the board, we should reflect that in pricing and a separate operational SOW.

5) Audit and evidence: If credits are disputed, Customer must submit a written claim within 30 days of the incident and Redwood will provide telemetry summaries, token-level logs where permitted, and the RCA. We should avoid unlimited discovery obligations.

I'll attach a redline of the Order Form language and proposed credit table. If Acme wants to keep 30-minute P1 for hosted, we should plan a support pricing adjustment.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime & maintenance windows — initial redlines

Lauren / Marcus — thank you for the fast turnaround and the detail. A couple follow-ups from Acme SREs: 

- For the credit exception clause: Acme is comfortable with a cap for ordinary incidents, but we want the exception path to be automatic (i.e., credits kick in once the 72-hour threshold is crossed) rather than discretionary. Post-incident RCA is fine for determining root cause afterwards, but we need clear, automatic triggers so we can keep internal finance forecasting stable.

- Emergency maintenance: We need a short-run playbook in the Order Form that describes our failover expectations (e.g., Redwood must publish maintenance region schedule, provide automated traffic routing guidance, and offer a temporary read-only mode where possible).

- P1 acknowledgement: To avoid price friction, Acme prefers the 30-minute acknowledgement for Dedicated now but is open to a short-term amendment to pilot 30-minute for hosted endpoints for the first 6 months post-go-live. We can accept an uplift if necessary.

Would appreciate if Marcus can share the maintenance matrix (per-region windows, notification cadence) and a suggested credit table mapping outage minutes to percentage credits so our procurement can model cost impact. We can meet Thu 15:00 EST to review if that slot is still open.

Regards,
Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime & maintenance windows — initial redlines (next steps)

Sarah — great, thanks. Quick confirmation of next steps and what I uploaded to the Drive link above: 

1) Maintenance matrix: uploaded a proposed staggered regional schedule (US-East, US-West, EU, APAC) with non-overlapping maintenance windows and 48–72h notice for standard changes, emergency notification path documented. See Drive: https://drive.redwood/Acme/SLA-proposals/202611

2) Credit table: attached in the RW_SLA_proposal_v3_redline.docx — it's a sliding scale (minutes -> % of monthly invoice) with an automatic trigger for credits once cumulative unplanned downtime >72 hours in any rolling 90-day window; legal retains post-incident RCA gating for exceptional additional relief (non-discretionary base credits are automatic).

3) Pilot for 30-minute P1 on hosted: we can run a 6-month pilot priced as an add-on. I'll put together SOW language and a one-page pricing addendum.

4) Meeting: Thu 15:00 EST confirmed for a 30m technical + procurement sync. I’ll send calendar invite and dial-in.

If legal (Lauren) is OK with the automated trigger language in the doc, we’ll circulate an updated Order Form redline later today.

Thanks — talk Thu.
- Marcus
